task.description:
Idiom/scope hard gate on the full ISS-0480 diff on this branch: `git diff origin/main...HEAD` (or `git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0480-20260905`). This is the standard REVIEWER gate per WF-03 Step 3 (same procedure as WF-02 2c/2d) -- it runs AFTER SECURITY-REVIEWER when SECURITY-REVIEWER is in scope, but ELIXIR-DEV's own stated judgement (confirmed twice, once per implementation attempt) is that this diff is OUT of SECURITY-REVIEWER's scope: it touches only test/support/, test/test_helper.exs, config/test.exs, and scripts/test_parallel.sh -- zero lib/letflow/ production code, zero migrations, zero API routes, zero tenant-data paths. Independently confirm this scope judgement yourself before proceeding as the sole gate (do not merely accept it) -- if you disagree, say so and route back to ORCH for a SECURITY-REVIEWER dispatch rather than silently proceeding.

The diff spans two design iterations: the core structural fix (new test/support/provisioning_repo.ex module, test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's provisioned_tenant!/1 redirected via put_dynamic_repo/1, config/test.exs and scripts/test_parallel.sh's pool-budget extension, test/test_helper.exs boot sequencing -- design §10.0-10.7) plus a narrow follow-on (design §10.8: two named test files' own local helpers wired through the same seam) added after a rework cycle when real execution found the first cut incomplete. Both CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate iterations (handoffs/WF03-ISS0480-20260905/step-02b-code-design-validator.json, both entries in gate_history plus the current result) independently verified the design against real Ecto/DBConnection source and real pool arithmetic -- you are not re-deriving those claims from scratch, but you ARE independently checking that the SHIPPED CODE actually matches what was designed and gated, which is a different question a design gate cannot answer.

Check specifically:
1. Idiomatic OTP/Elixir usage in test/support/provisioning_repo.ex and the with_provisioning_repo/1 seam in tenant_fixture.ex -- does the try/after actually guarantee restoration of the previous dynamic repo even if fun.() raises? Read it directly.
2. Scope creep -- does the diff touch anything beyond what design §10/§10.8 specify? Any stray file, any unrelated refactor bundled in?
3. Consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ records -- does this change contradict any existing decision record (0009 is the one most likely to interact; both CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gates already checked its arithmetic, but check whether the SHIPPED config/test.exs and scripts/test_parallel.sh changes match what was gated, not just whether the arithmetic itself is sound).
4. Whether the two §10.8 exception-case edits (tenant_fixture_test.exs's hard_cleanup/1, promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs's provisioned_tenant/0) are the narrowest correct fix or whether they read as a workaround that should instead have prompted revisiting the core design -- your own independent judgement call, since ELIXIR-DEV/CODE-DESIGNER already made this call once and you are the next independent check on it.
5. No supervision-tree file touched (lib/letflow/process_instance.ex, instance_supervisor.ex, or similar) -- confirm by checking the diff's file list directly.

This is a hard gate. A PASS must state what you independently checked and how (read the code, ran a check), not merely 'looks fine.'
acceptance_criteria: SECURITY-REVIEWER scope judgement independently confirmed or refuted with reasoning
with_provisioning_repo/1's exception-safety (try/after) verified by direct code read
No scope creep found, or named specifically if found
Consistency with decision 0009 confirmed by checking shipped config/test.exs and scripts/test_parallel.sh against what was gated, not merely re-trusting the arithmetic
Independent judgement on whether the §10.8 exception-case edits are the narrowest correct fix
No supervision-tree file touched, confirmed by checking the diff's file list directly
Any BLOCKER named specifically enough to act on without further clarification
